overview: EBOS Group is the largest and most diversified Australasian marketer, wholesaler, and distributor of healthcare, medical, and pharmaceutical products, with a leading position in animal care distribution. With over 5,700 employees across Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, EBOS operates through two main segments: Healthcare (pharmaceutical wholesale, hospital distribution, medical technology including spine and oncology, retail pharmacy networks TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice, contract logistics) and Animal Care (branded pet foods including Black Hawk and VitaPet, and veterinary supplies distribution via Lyppard and SVS). The company is dual-listed on the NZX and ASX and reports in Australian dollars.

business_model.summary: EBOS operates a diversified distribution and retail model with approximately 93% of revenue from Healthcare and 7% from Animal Care (H1 FY2026 actuals). Revenue is generated through wholesale distribution margins regulated by PBS/PHARMAC frameworks, retail pharmacy franchise operations, medical technology partnerships, branded product sales in animal care, and contract logistics services.

revenue_streams.name: Community Pharmacy Wholesale
revenue_streams.description: Distribution to independent pharmacies in Australia and New Zealand. Revenue A$3,610M in H1 FY2026, up 14.8% YoY. Growth driven by GLP-1 and high-value medicines. GOR margin 8.6% (down 60bps due to high-value medicine cap structure and competitive dynamics ahead of expanded CSO regime from July 2026).

revenue_streams.name: Institutional Healthcare
revenue_streams.description: Distribution to hospitals and aged care (medicines/consumables A$1,893M, up 2%), plus Medical Technology (A$337M, up 12.1% in H1 FY2026). MedTech growing through spine, urology, oncology, and Southeast Asia expansion. GOR margin improved 30bps to 15.6%.

revenue_streams.name: Contract Logistics
revenue_streams.description: 3PL/4PL services including clinical trial logistics, cold chain. GOR grew 13.5% to A$86M in H1 FY2026. 12 net new principal wins. New Perth facility nearing completion. High-value medicines and temperature-controlled storage driving growth.

revenue_streams.name: Animal Care - Branded Products
revenue_streams.description: Branded pet foods (Black Hawk #1 premium pet food in ANZ, VitaPet) and treats. Revenue A$177M in H1 FY2026, up 5.8%. Supported by new product launches (freeze-dried, air-dried treats) and in-house manufacturing from NextGen acquisition.

revenue_streams.name: Animal Care - Wholesale
revenue_streams.description: Veterinary wholesale distribution via Lyppard and SVS (acquired March 2025). Revenue doubled to A$274M in H1 FY2026 driven by SVS contribution. Strong SVS integration and Lyppard share gains.

business_model.customer_type: B2B primarily (pharmacies, hospitals, veterinary clinics, retailers) with B2C through TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice pharmacy networks
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia 75% (A$5,107M in H1 FY2026), New Zealand and others 25% (A$1,660M). Australia healthcare EBITDA margin 4.2%, NZ and SEA 3.3% in H1 FY2026.
business_model.margin_profile: Wholesale distribution GOR margins: community pharmacy 8.6% (H1 FY2026), institutional healthcare 15.6%, contract logistics GOR A$86M. Animal Care EBITDA margin 15.1% (underlying, H1 FY2026). Overall underlying EBITDA margin 4.4% in H1 FY2026 (down 50bps from 4.9% in H1 FY2025), reflecting DC transition costs and elevated D&A. CSO regime expansion from July 2026 expected to support improved GOR margin in H2 FY2026 and beyond.

main_competitors: Sigma Healthcare (merged with Chemist Warehouse in 2024-2025, ~35-40% pharmacy wholesale market share)
API (owned by Wesfarmers since 2022, operates Priceline Pharmacy network)
National Veterinary Care (NVS) in animal health
Greencross (owned by TPG Capital) in pet retail and veterinary services
DHL Supply Chain / Toll Group in healthcare contract logistics
competitive_position.market_position: Largest healthcare distributor in Australia and New Zealand by network breadth. Leading position in hospital distribution and medical technology (spine implantables). TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice combined form a 782-store pharmacy retail network (630 TWC + 81 MediAdvice + 71 other brands as at Dec 2025). In animal care, EBOS holds the #1 position in premium dry dog food in ANZ pet specialty through Black Hawk.
competitive_position.market_share: Approximately 30-35% of pharmaceutical wholesale market in ANZ following Chemist Warehouse contract loss. Post-CSO expansion and GLP-1 growth, EBOS is consolidating its position with independent pharmacies. Sigma-Chemist Warehouse entity holds 35-40% of the Australian wholesale market. EBOS is the #1 surgical implantables partner in APAC for Medical Technology.

moat_factors.description: A$360 million investment in eight new/upgraded distribution centres (2022-2026) with six of eight sites now operational. Largest and most complex site (Symbion Kemps Creek) went live October 2025 on-time and on-budget. New Perth facility nearing completion. State-of-the-art cold chain and specialty medicine capabilities (critical for GLP-1 and biologics) with automated systems. These assets represent significant barriers to entry and a long-term operational cost advantage.

Pharmaceutical wholesale requires extensive licensing, Good Distribution Practice (GDP) compliance, controlled substance permits, and temperature-controlled logistics capabilities. EBOS's participation in the Australian PBS Community Service Obligation (CSO) framework and New Zealand PHARMAC distribution arrangements provides contractual certainty and regulated revenue streams. The expanded CSO regime from July 2026 (covering Section 100 Medicines) enhances EBOS's position.

As the largest healthcare distributor in ANZ, EBOS benefits from economies of scale in logistics, procurement, and systems. The breadth of service across community pharmacy, hospital, medical technology, contract logistics, and animal care creates cross-selling and bundling opportunities unavailable to smaller competitors.

Long-term relationships with hospitals, pharmacies, and veterinary clinics. Integration of ordering/inventory systems creates switching costs. TerryWhite Chemmart (630 stores) and MediAdvice (81 stores) pharmacy networks have multi-year commitments. Retained key customer contracts despite competitive wholesale landscape in H1 FY2026.

moat_factors.factor: Vertical integration across healthcare value chain
moat_factors.description: Ownership of wholesale distribution (Symbion), medical technology distribution, retail pharmacy networks (TWC, MediAdvice), contract logistics, and animal care manufacturing/distribution creates synergies unavailable to single-segment players. TWC Consumer Brands (300+ products) and TWC Retail Media (digital screens) open new revenue streams.

Black Hawk is the leading premium pet food in ANZ by volume in pet specialty. VitaPet is a leading pet treat brand in NZ supermarkets. In-house manufacturing capability from NextGen acquisition enables innovation (freeze-dried, air-dried formats) to defend and grow brand share. SVS brand also recognised as an indefinite-life intangible (A$38.4M).

Consolidation of Origin Biologics (ABT Nevada LLC) in December 2025 deepens the allograft biologics offering. Potential to replicate Australian allograft success in the US market. AlphaXRT acquisition expands into radiation oncology, a new therapy channel. Biologics and MedTech are structurally higher-margin businesses within the group.

weaknesses: Lost Chemist Warehouse wholesale contract in Australia (A$1.9 billion annual revenue, ~10% of group) to Sigma in 2024, demonstrating vulnerability to large customer contract losses in a competitive market
Regulated wholesale GOR margins under 1PWA framework (cap on high-value medicines) limit upside in community pharmacy despite strong volume growth; structural feature until next agreement negotiation
Elevated DC transition costs and D&A in FY2026 are depressing near-term margins and free cash flow, creating a period of heightened investor scrutiny
Fuel and consumable cost exposure: April 2026 guidance downgrade to A$610-620M EBITDA (from A$615-635M) highlights inability to pass through fuel cost increases quickly due to government contracts
Geographic concentration - primarily exposed to Australia and New Zealand economies with limited international diversification beyond early-stage Southeast Asia
Animal Care segment GOR margin diluted by SVS wholesale acquisition (lower-margin business), reducing segment comparability and masking branded product margin quality

growth_drivers: GLP-1 and high-value medicine structural growth: GLP-1 (semaglutide) volumes grew ~230% since FY2022 and now represent ~2% of PBS spend (up from 0.8%). High-value medicines represent 39% of total PBS spend at $7.6bn despite being <1% of script volumes, driving average prescription price to $58.1. EBOS directly benefits through expanded cold storage and specialty logistics capability. CSO expansion to Section 100 Medicines from July 2026 is an additional positive.

DC renewal program delivering operational leverage: Six of eight sites complete (including largest Kemps Creek, on time/budget, October 2025). Remaining Perth and Onelink Auckland sites due FY2026. Full network automation benefits expected to flow through FY2027-FY2028, removing duplication, improving throughput, and delivering cost efficiency. Capex expected to decline ~30% in FY2027, unlocking significantly improved free cash flow.

Medical Technology expansion in ANZ and Southeast Asia: MedTech revenue grew 12.1% in H1 FY2026 (7.7% organic). Spine, urology, neurosurgery, neurovascular intervention all growing. AlphaXRT (radiation oncology) and Precision Surgical (spine, NSW east coast) acquisitions expand therapy areas and geography. SEA expansion ongoing. Origin Biologics consolidation provides US growth optionality.

Retail pharmacy network expansion and monetisation: 782-store network (630 TWC + 81 MediAdvice + 71 other) as at December 2025, up 89 net stores in H1 FY2026. TWC same-store sales up 8.8%, dispensary up 10.4%. TWC Consumer Brands (300+ products), TWC CareClinics (vaccination, prescribing), and TWC Connect Retail Media (200 new digital screens across 100 stores) are new and growing revenue streams.

Animal Care growth and manufacturing capability: SVS integration progressing well, bringing cross-division productivity. NextGen (Queensland pet treat manufacturer) expands into new formats (air-dried, freeze-dried). Kiwi Kitchens and VitaPet innovation continuing. Pet humanisation trend structurally supports premium pet food and veterinary services growth. Animal Care EBITDA growing 15.1% in H1 FY2026.

CSO expanded regime from July 2026: The Australian Government's expanded CSO framework covering Section 100 Medicines from 1 July 2026 and an increased cap for high-cost medicines (from A$54 to A$223 per script) is expected to support improved GOR growth and GOR margin in H2 FY2026 and FY2027. Management highlighted this as a material positive.

Bolt-on M&A pipeline remains active: Strategy of disciplined bolt-on acquisitions to expand regional presence and therapeutic areas. Each deal expected to be EPS accretive and deliver ROCE above Group hurdle rate. Pipeline is active across Medical Technology, Retail Pharmacy, and Animal Care.

Medium-term EBITDA growth target: At the April 2026 Investor Day, management outlined targets of mid-single-digit organic underlying EBITDA growth over the medium term, supported by DC automation benefits, improved utilisation, mix shift to higher-margin businesses (MedTech, branded Animal Care), and efficiencies from network scale.

business.risk: Loss of major customers or contracts
business.description: Loss of Chemist Warehouse wholesale contract (A$1.9B revenue, ~10% of group) in 2024 demonstrated customer concentration risk. While EBOS won substantial new pharmacy customers, major contract losses can materially impact revenue and margins. Pharmacy wholesale remains competitive with Sigma-Chemist Warehouse (35-40% market share) aggressively competing for independent pharmacies.

H1 FY2026 saw Healthcare EBITDA margin decline 40bps to 4.0% due to DC transition costs, heightened competition, and the 1PWA cap structure on high-value medicines limiting GOR margin capture despite strong volume growth. Community pharmacy GOR margin declined 60bps to 8.6%. While the CSO expansion from July 2026 is expected to support margins, structural margin pressure from the 1PWA framework persists until the next agreement cycle.

In April 2026, EBOS downgraded FY2026 underlying EBITDA guidance to A$610-620M (from A$615-635M) due to elevated fuel prices and hydrocarbon-related consumables (plastic wrapping, polystyrene foam) from geopolitical disruptions. The distribution-intensive nature of the business limits ability to pass costs through immediately due to government contracts. Discussions with the Australian Government on fuel cost recovery are ongoing with uncertain outcome.

Pharmaceutical distributors depend on maintaining relationships with major pharmaceutical manufacturers. Loss of key supplier distribution rights could impact revenue. Limited number of generic drug suppliers in the ANZ market.

Sigma-Chemist Warehouse merger (2024-2025) creates the largest vertically integrated pharmacy player in Australia with 35-40% wholesale market share. API-Priceline (owned by Wesfarmers) is another vertically integrated competitor with deep capital resources. These competitors may leverage retail scale to pressure wholesale pricing and independent pharmacy loyalty.

Ongoing PBS price reforms in Australia and PHARMAC pricing pressures in New Zealand reduce drug prices over time, though GLP-1 and specialty medicine volume and value growth largely offsets this. PBS total expenditure continues to grow year-on-year driven by high-value medicines.

financial.risk: Debt levels and leverage during peak investment cycle
financial.description: Net debt at A$1,121M as at December 2025, leverage 2.2x (within target range of 1.7-2.3x). Leverage increased due to DC renewal program investment and bolt-on M&A. Free cash flow was negative in H1 FY2026 (reported FCF -A$24M) due to working capital timing effects and elevated capex. Leverage expected to reduce from FY2027 as capex falls ~30% and EBITDA grows.

EBOS reports in Australian dollars but the parent company is incorporated in New Zealand (NZX listed). NZD dividends are declared then converted to AUD for payment. AUD/NZD exchange rate fluctuations impact reported NZD earnings and dividend values. The foreign currency translation reserve deteriorated A$48.8M in H1 FY2026, reflecting AUD weakness against NZD. Revenue is ~75% AUD and ~25% NZD, creating a natural hedge on operations.

financial.risk: Working capital intensity and cash conversion
financial.description: Net working capital increased A$84M in H1 FY2026 to A$507M, supporting revenue growth and DC transition activities. H1 FY2026 underlying cash flow before capex was only A$66M (vs A$205M in H1 FY2025), impacted by the unwind of ~A$50M prior period timing benefits and ~A$75M one-time Chemist Warehouse working capital release in the prior period. Cash conversion days increased 1.5 days to 20.7 days.

EBOS has deployed ~A$2B into higher-growth segments over the past five years. H1 FY2026 acquisitions include NGPF, Precision Surgical, AlphaXRT, MediAdvice, and consolidation of Origin Biologics - each requiring integration execution. Goodwill now stands at A$2.28B. Elevated restructuring and site transition costs (A$20M underlying adjustment in H1 FY2026) reflect the cost of the transformation program.

regulatory.description: The Australian First Pharmacy Wholesaler Agreement (1PWA) caps GOR margins structurally, with the cap on high-value medicines limiting revenue capture despite volume growth. The expanded CSO from July 2026 (Section 100 Medicines) and increased high-cost medicine cap (A$54 to A$223) are partial mitigants but the fundamental pricing structure requires government negotiation for material change. PHARMAC in New Zealand similarly constrains pricing.

Australia maintains pharmacy ownership rules restricting non-pharmacist ownership. Potential regulatory changes could disrupt the TerryWhite Chemmart and MediAdvice retail model. PBS distribution and location rules could also change, affecting the competitive landscape.

Increasing proportion of specialty and high-value medicines require strict temperature control and GDP compliance. Regulatory requirements are stringent. Compliance failures could result in license suspension, product recalls, and reputational damage. The DC renewal program is partly designed to address these requirements.

regulatory.risk: Fuel cost recovery from Australian Government
regulatory.description: EBOS is in discussions with the Australian Government regarding recovery of elevated fuel and hydrocarbon-related costs in the healthcare distribution supply chain. Outcome and timing uncertain. Government CSO funding arrangements may not adequately compensate for cost increases in the near term.

macro.description: EBOS revenues are tied to government healthcare spending through PBS and PHARMAC. Budget constraints could accelerate generic substitution or reduce reimbursement rates. However, aging demographics and rising chronic disease prevalence provide structural demand support that is difficult to curtail.

macro.risk: Consumer discretionary spending in Animal Care
macro.description: Animal Care segment (~7% of revenue, but higher EBITDA margin contribution) is exposed to consumer spending on premium pet food and veterinary services. Economic recession or cost-of-living pressures could drive trading down to value brands, impacting branded product margins. The SVS wholesale acquisition has partially diluted segment margin, reducing overall sensitivity.

macro.risk: Global supply disruptions and geopolitical risks
macro.description: The April 2026 guidance downgrade explicitly cited global supply disruptions and geopolitical risks (Middle East conflict) driving fuel price increases and elevated costs for hydrocarbon-related consumables. International logistics disruptions (shipping, air freight) could also impact pharmaceutical supply chain availability and costs.

Net finance costs were A$58M in H1 FY2026, expected to be at the top-end of the A$110-120M full-year guidance range following the increase in the Australian cash rate and additional debt funding for H1 FY2026 acquisitions. Higher-for-longer rates increase interest costs and pressure consumer spending in Animal Care.

Australia and New Zealand rely on imported pharmaceuticals and medical supplies. International logistics disruptions could impact product availability. EBOS's DC investment program improves domestic logistics resilience.

execution.risk: DC renewal program final sites and ramp-up
execution.description: Six of eight DC renewal sites are now operational. Remaining Perth (Contract Logistics) and Onelink Auckland sites targeted for completion by end of FY2026, with post-commissioning workstreams including IT systems and optimisation continuing into H1 FY2027. Full network benefits (automation, productivity, duplication removal) expected to flow progressively over FY2027-FY2028. Transition costs elevated (~A$20M restructuring/site transition in H1 FY2026).

Adam Hall took over as CEO in July 2025 after John Cullity's retirement. His first half-year results (H1 FY2026) were solid operationally and the April 2026 Investor Day demonstrated strategic clarity. The April 2026 guidance downgrade due to fuel costs was the first material miss under Hall's tenure, though underlying demand remains stable.

EBOS completed five acquisitions in H1 FY2026 (NGPF, Precision Surgical, AlphaXRT, MediAdvice, and Origin Biologics step acquisition), with combined upfront consideration of ~A$70M. Each requires integration to achieve synergy targets. M&A transaction costs were A$3M and restructuring costs A$20M in H1 FY2026. Track record is generally positive but execution risk accumulates with deal volume.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Healthcare distribution in Australia and New Zealand benefits from strong structural tailwinds: aging demographics, rising PBS expenditure (driven by high-value and specialty medicines), GLP-1 volume growth (~230% since FY2022), and increasing medical technology adoption. Industry pharmaceutical wholesale revenue growing above historical trend driven by high-value medicine volumes. Pet care industry growing 5-7% annually driven by pet humanisation and premiumisation. Medical Technology in ANZ and SEA is a high-growth segment with EBOS well positioned through recent acquisitions.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate cyclicality. Pharmaceutical distribution is defensive with stable, government-funded demand through economic cycles. Animal Care branded segment has moderate cyclical exposure. Overall business is relatively recession-resistant, though premium pet food can see trading-down in downturns.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate sensitivity. EBOS carries net debt of A$1,121M (leverage 2.2x) so higher rates increase interest costs. The Australian cash rate increase during FY2026 pushed net finance costs to the top-end of guidance. Consumer spending in Animal Care is rate-sensitive. Healthcare spending generally less sensitive.
key_input_costs: Fuel and transport costs (elevated in FY2026 due to geopolitical supply disruptions, caused April 2026 guidance downgrade)
Hydrocarbon-related consumables (plastic wrapping, polystyrene foam for cold chain packaging)
Labor costs (5,700+ employees, logistics workers facing wage inflation in Australia)
Energy costs (cold chain storage and new DC facilities are energy-intensive)
Technology and systems investments (warehouse automation, digital platforms, IT cutover for DC program)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Reports in Australian dollars. Parent company incorporated in NZ and listed on NZX; dividends declared in NZD (NZ 57.0 cps interim, maintained). AUD/NZD rate movement impacts NZD-translated earnings and dividend values for NZ investors. Foreign currency translation reserve deteriorated A$48.8M in H1 FY2026, reflecting AUD weakness. Revenue is approximately 75% AUD, 25% NZD providing a natural partial hedge on operations.

recent_developments.event: FY2026 underlying EBITDA guidance downgraded to A$610-620M (from A$615-635M) due to elevated fuel prices and hydrocarbon-related consumable costs from global supply disruptions and geopolitical risks. Estimated additional cost impact of A$5-10M absorbed in FY2026. Australian Government discussions on fuel cost recovery ongoing with uncertain outcome. Management stated impact limited to FY2026 with mitigation efforts underway for FY2027.

Investor Day held in Sydney. EBOS outlined medium-term strategy including: mid-single-digit organic underlying EBITDA growth targets, ~30% capex reduction from FY2027 supporting stronger free cash flow and EPS growth from FY2028, dividend payout ratio of 60-80% of underlying NPAT, and redeployment of ~A$2B into higher-growth segments (MedTech, Animal Care) over the prior five years. DC automation benefits expected to drive operational leverage from FY2027-FY2028.

H1 FY2026 results released: Revenue A$6,767.7M (+13.0%), statutory EBITDA A$302.7M (+9.7%), underlying EBITDA A$300M (+3.2%), statutory EPS 61.1 cents (+7.4%), interim dividend NZ 57.0 cents maintained. FY2026 full-year underlying EBITDA guidance of A$615-635M reaffirmed at this point. H2 FY2026 EBITDA guided at A$315-335M, implying meaningful uplift from H1.

Consolidated control of Origin Biologics (previously ABT Nevada LLC, US allograft solutions business) through step acquisition. Previously 51%-owned but equity-accounted as associate. Remeasurement gain of A$21.3M recognised. A$38.1M financial liability recognised for pathway to 100% ownership. Opens US market growth optionality for allograft biologics.

Bank facility refinancing completed: A$300M facility (due December 2026) refinanced to A$400M facility maturing December 2032. Weighted average debt maturity extended to 3.3 years (from 2.9 years at June 2025). Undrawn committed facilities of ~A$930M providing strong liquidity headroom.

Acquired AlphaXRT (radiation oncology solutions, ANZ) and Precision Surgical (spine implants, NSW east coast) for combined ~A$27M upfront plus earnouts. Expand Medical Technology therapy areas and geographic presence.

Largest and most complex DC renewal site, Symbion Kemps Creek (Sydney), went live on-time and on-budget. Six of eight DC renewal sites now operational. Productivity and utilisation expected to improve progressively through H2 FY2026 and into FY2027.

Acquired majority interest in MediAdvice, a NSW pharmacy management company with ~80 pharmacies, in H1 FY2026. Added 81 stores to retail pharmacy network. MediAdvice to remain a separate banner focused on innovative community care. Total retail pharmacy network grew to 782 stores (89 net adds in H1 FY2026).

FY2025 full-year results and FY2026 guidance issued. Adam Hall's first results as CEO. Revenue A$12.3B, underlying EBITDA in line with guidance. FY2026 underlying EBITDA guided at A$615-635M (~7% midpoint growth), slightly weighted to H2.

Next Generation Pet Foods (Queensland pet treat manufacturer, A$43M) acquisition completed. Adds multi-format pet treat manufacturing including air-dried capability, expanding Animal Care manufacturing footprint.
Adam Hall became CEO effective 1 July 2025, succeeding John Cullity who retired after 7+ years as CEO. Hall is an internal appointment with strong background in EBOS operations.

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Results (25 February 2026) and Investor Day (30 April 2026); guidance downgrade issued 22 April 2026

items.notes: Downgraded on 22 April 2026 from A$615-635M (reaffirmed at February H1 results). Reflects estimated A$5-10M additional fuel and hydrocarbon consumable cost impact. H1 FY2026 delivered A$300M underlying EBITDA, implying H2 FY2026 of A$310-320M. New midpoint is A$615M (~5% growth from FY2025 base of ~A$585M).

items.target: A$315-335 million (at time of H1 results, pre-downgrade)
items.period: H2 FY2026 (Jul-Dec 2026 equivalent; EBOS FY Jun year-end)
items.notes: Uplift of A$21-41M from H2 FY2025. Confidence based on: productivity uplift as Kemps Creek ramps, mix support from Medical Technology, expanded CSO regime from July 2026, reduced DC transition one-offs, and cost discipline programs. April fuel cost downgrade modestly reduces the range.
H1 FY2026 D&A was A$67M (underlying). H2 FY2026 expected to be higher than H1. Reflects ongoing investment in DC renewal program. Expected to normalise on a more stable asset base from FY2027.

items.target: At top-end of A$110-120 million range
items.notes: H1 FY2026 net finance costs were A$58M. Expected to be at top-end of range due to Australian cash rate increase plus A$1-2M additional from H1 FY2026 acquisition funding.
H1 FY2026 underlying effective tax rate was 27.5%, on track.

items.target: A$130-140 million (FY2026, plus A$6M safety uplift)
items.notes: H1 FY2026 capex was A$70M. An additional A$6M safety-related spend added to original A$130-140M guidance. FY2027 capex expected to be ~30% lower on a comparable basis, as DC renewal program concludes.

items.vs_prior: new guidance provided at Investor Day
items.notes: Announced at 30 April 2026 Investor Day. Supported by DC automation benefits, utilisation improvements, business mix shift toward MedTech and branded Animal Care, and pharmacy network scale. EPS growth from FY2028 as D&A and interest normalise.

H1 FY2026 interim dividend was NZ 57.0 cents per share (maintained vs prior year). H1 FY2026 payout ratio was 82% of underlying NPAT, reflecting Board confidence in medium-term earnings outlook. DRP operated at 2.0% discount.

items.target: Target range 1.7-2.3x; expected to deleverage from FY2027
items.notes: Leverage at 2.2x as at December 2025 (within target range). Deleveraging expected in FY2027 as capex falls, EBITDA grows, and free cash flow improves materially.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Adam Hall stated that EBOS remains a defensive growth company focused on care, productivity, and partnerships. At the Investor Day, Hall outlined confidence in medium-term growth through DC automation benefits, expanded pharmacy network monetisation, Medical Technology geographic and therapy expansion, and Animal Care brand innovation. The April 2026 fuel cost guidance downgrade was attributed to external factors beyond EBOS's control, with demand across the portfolio remaining stable. Management is pursuing fuel cost efficiency measures and government discussions for recovery, with benefits expected to flow through in FY2027. CFO Alistair Gray highlighted that peak investment is now complete and FY2027 will represent a meaningful step-up in free cash flow generation.

bull_case: DC program completing and creating multi-year operational leverage: Six of eight sites done, with Kemps Creek (largest) on-time and on-budget. FY2027 capex falls ~30%, removing the single biggest headwind to free cash flow and EPS growth. Automation benefits, productivity uplift, and duplication removal provide a structural cost advantage that compounds from FY2027-FY2028. The investment case is essentially a coiled spring ready to release.

GLP-1 and high-value medicine structural tailwind uniquely positions EBOS: GLP-1 volumes grew 230% since FY2022 and are now 2% of PBS spend (up from 0.8%). High-value medicines are 39% of PBS expenditure at only <1% of scripts, driving average prescription price to A$58.1. EBOS has invested specifically in expanded cold storage and temperature-controlled logistics for this category. The expanded CSO regime from July 2026 (Section 100 Medicines) provides regulatory income support.

Medical Technology platform accelerating: MedTech revenue grew 12.1% in H1 FY2026 (7.7% organic) with GOR margin improving to 15.6%. AlphaXRT (oncology) and Precision Surgical (spine) expand therapy and geography. Origin Biologics consolidation opens US market for allograft biologics. MedTech is structurally higher-margin than pharmaceutical wholesale, and continued mix shift improves group profitability over time. EBOS is #1 surgical implantables partner in APAC.

Pharmacy network expansion creating new high-margin revenue streams: 782-store network with TWC dispensary same-store sales up 10.4% and total TWC network sales A$1.5B (+9.8%). TWC Consumer Brands (300+ products), TWC CareClinics (vaccination, pharmacist prescribing), TWC Retail Media, and MediAdvice innovative care model provide growing, higher-margin revenue beyond traditional wholesale. Network expected to grow toward 800+ stores.

Fuel cost headwind is transient, not structural: The April 2026 guidance downgrade was A$5-10M on a base of ~A$615M EBITDA - a ~1% impact. Management explicitly characterised it as FY2026-specific, with mitigation measures underway and government discussions on cost recovery. The underlying business delivered 13% revenue growth and stable demand. Once fuel normalises and mitigation takes effect, the headwind reverses.

Investor Day validates FY2027+ inflection story: Mid-single-digit EBITDA growth targets, ~30% capex reduction, EPS growth from FY2028, and 60-80% dividend payout ratio provide a clear financial roadmap. The A$2B redeployment into higher-margin segments (MedTech, Animal Care) over five years is beginning to shift the group's margin profile. Balance sheet leverage within target at 2.2x with strong liquidity (~A$930M undrawn).

Defensive business model with structural demographic tailwinds: Healthcare distribution is non-cyclical with stable government funding (PBS, PHARMAC). Aging ANZ population drives 3%+ annual pharmaceutical volume growth. Pet humanisation trend supports premium Animal Care. Business is well-diversified across community pharmacy, hospital, MedTech, contract logistics, and animal care - no single segment represents more than 53% of revenue.
bear_case: FY2026 guidance downgrade signals cost structure vulnerability: The April 2026 downgrade (A$5-10M fuel impact) reveals that EBOS's cost structure is exposed to external shocks it cannot easily pass through due to government contracts. The inability to recover fuel and consumable cost increases quickly is a structural weakness in the distribution model. A prolonged period of elevated energy costs or further geopolitical disruption could exacerbate this.

Margin compression persists despite strong revenue growth: Healthcare EBITDA margin fell 40bps to 4.0% in H1 FY2026 even with 13% revenue growth. Underlying EBITDA margin fell 50bps to 4.4%. Community pharmacy GOR margin declined 60bps to 8.6% due to the 1PWA cap structure on high-value medicines. DC transition costs (A$20M restructuring/site transition in H1 FY2026) and elevated D&A (+21% to A$67M) are compressing reported earnings. This disconnect between revenue growth and margin expansion is a concern.

Elevated leverage and negative free cash flow during transition: Net debt rose to A$1,121M (2.2x leverage at top of target range). Reported FCF was -A$24M in H1 FY2026. The near-term earnings power is being absorbed by the DC investment program and D&A. Dividend payout ratio was 82% of underlying NPAT on a cash dividend basis, leaving limited reinvestment headroom. If EBITDA growth disappoints, leverage could breach covenants.

FY2026 represents peak year of multiple headwinds stacking: DC transition costs, elevated D&A and capex, Australian interest rate increases, fuel cost inflation, and community pharmacy GOR margin pressure are all coinciding in FY2026. While management characterises these as transient, the timing uncertainty of DC ramp-up, fuel recovery, and CSO benefits means FY2026 earnings may disappoint further.

Customer contract concentration risk remains after Chemist Warehouse: Having lost A$1.9B (10% of group revenue) to Sigma in 2024, EBOS has rebuilt partially through new independent pharmacy customers. But the market remains competitive and any further major contract loss could repeat the earnings hit. The Sigma-Chemist Warehouse entity (35-40% wholesale share) is a formidable competitor with integrated retail leverage.

Animal Care segment margin dilution and integration complexity: The acquisition of SVS (NZ vet wholesale, March 2025) nearly doubled Animal Care revenue but compressed GOR margin from 34.7% to 27.4% because SVS is a lower-margin wholesale business. This makes the segment's financial profile less attractive on a per-dollar basis. Integration of five acquisitions (NGPF, AlphaXRT, Precision Surgical, MediAdvice, Origin Biologics) in a single half creates execution risk.

FY2027 recovery priced into consensus: Analyst consensus maintains a Buy rating with average NZD price targets of ~NZ$33-38, implying the FY2027 free cash flow inflection is already captured in valuations. If the DC automation benefits materialise more slowly than guided (post-commissioning workstreams extend into H1 FY2027), or if fuel/cost pressures persist, the multiple could compress further before the earnings recovery arrives.
